behavior_anomalies.why: Hospitalized patients receive care and progress despite hospital occupied_beds having started at zero, with no logged admission or increase in occupancy.

behavior_anomalies.quote: t2 clinical-staff did assess-ventilation-need-v1: hospitalized-flu-patients.patient_group.ventilation_status not ventilated->needs ventilation
behavior_anomalies.why: A patient develops a ventilation need despite zero initial occupied beds and no logged admission establishing an occupied patient population.

behavior_anomalies.quote: t6 clinical-staff did assign-ventilators-by-staff-v1: hospital-ventilators.ventilator_stock.in_use_count 0->1; hospitalized-flu-patients.patient_group.ventilation_status needs ventilation->ventilated
behavior_anomalies.why: A hospitalized patient is assigned a ventilator even though occupancy began at zero and no increase in occupied beds is shown.

behavior_anomalies.quote:
t6 process functional-ventilators-fail: hospital-ventilators.ventilator_stock.functional_count 1->0
t6 clinical-staff did assign-ventilators-by-staff-v1: hospital-ventilators.ventilator_stock.in_use_count 0->1; hospitalized-flu-patients.patient_group.ventilation_status needs ventilation->ventilated
behavior_anomalies.why: A ventilator is assigned and the patient becomes ventilated immediately after functional_count reaches zero. This is physically implausible because no functional ventilator is available, and in_use_count increases to one despite zero usable units.

The log completes a ventilator-use cycle for a patient whose ventilator assignment occurred while functional_count was zero, without recording that the patient lost ventilation or otherwise accounting for the unavailable equipment.

The only ventilator is released, but the patient previously changed to `ventilated` and no corresponding transition away from ventilated status is recorded. The patient therefore remains ventilated with zero ventilators in use.

All functional ventilators are exhausted while the patient remains recorded as ventilated, yet no loss of ventilation or other consequence follows. Subsequent patient-care actions continue without resolving this impossible resource dependency.
The ventilator stock reaches zero, but the patient previously assigned a ventilator remains implicitly ventilated. No loss of ventilation, deterioration, transfer, or death is recorded.

The patient group's stay reaches zero while its ventilation status is never changed from ventilated. The patient therefore continues to depend on ventilation without a corresponding discharge, recovery, or death transition.

behavior_anomalies.quote:
t9 process functional-ventilators-fail: hospital-ventilators.ventilator_stock.functional_count 1->0
t9 clinical-staff did provide-patient-care-v1: clinical-staff.clinical_staff.daily_staff_capacity 120->119; hospitalized-flu-patients.patient_group.length_of_stay_remaining 5->4
behavior_anomalies.why: The hospital has zero functional ventilators, yet the patient previously marked ventilated continues receiving care and progressing toward recovery; no loss of ventilation or deterioration occurs.
Functional ventilators are exhausted, but no consequence for the patient still marked ventilated appears. The log continues patient care and recovery afterward, despite no ventilator support.

The ventilator use ends, but the patient status is never changed from ventilated. The patient later progresses from hospitalized to recovering and reaches zero remaining stay without any documented discharge or ventilation-status transition.
The functional ventilator resource reaches zero while a patient is already recorded as ventilated, but no loss of ventilation, deterioration, or other consequence for the dependent patient appears.

After repeated zero-functional-ventilator states, the ventilated patient continues receiving care and progressing toward discharge without any modeled consequence of having no functional ventilator available.
